name: The Comparison
description: Somebody names the usual way of doing it, then shows the alternative, then says which one they kept. A generated flat-lay of the two options sits between the two spoken beats, so the comparison is seen as well as claimed. For a brand whose buyer is already choosing between options and needs a reason, not an introduction.

theirs.description: The usual way, described the way somebody doing it would describe it — not a straw man.

ours.description: What this brand does instead, in one mechanical sentence.

verdict.description: The line that settles it, ending in the call to action.

presenter.description: Casting note, e.g. 'man, 30s, warehouse manager, hi-vis over a hoodie'.

value.frame: Shot on an iPhone front-facing camera, handheld, vertical 9:16, photorealistic. Realistic skin texture with visible pores, natural unevenness, no beauty filter. Available light from a window and a ceiling lamp, uneven shadows. Casual clothing with real creases. A real working space behind them with specific clutter. Slightly off-centre framing, mild lens distortion, subtle grain. Both eyes open, direct eye contact with the lens.
value.motion: Keep the exact same person, hair, wardrobe and room as the reference image. Handheld phone feel with slight drift. The person talks to camera and uses their hands to weigh one thing against the other. Natural blinking and breathing. Continuous phone footage, no cuts.
value.negative: eyes closed, mid-blink, looking away, head turned away, profile view, studio lighting, cinematic colour grade, airbrushed skin, plastic skin, beauty filter, CGI, 3D render, stock photo, polished commercial look, watermark, text overlay, subtitles, extra fingers, warped hands

nodes.system: You write comparison video for vertical feeds. You are fair to the other option — a comparison that mocks the alternative reads as an advert, and a comparison that describes it accurately reads as advice. You never name a competitor by name.

schema.actor: one paragraph pinning down age, build, hair, face, exact clothing and the specific room
schema.master_frame_prompt: still-image prompt for the opening frame
schema.open_edit_prompt: edit instruction for the sceptical opening beat
schema.verdict_edit_prompt: edit instruction for the closing beat
schema.compare_card_prompt: text-to-image prompt for an overhead flat-lay of the two options

nodes.prompt:
{{script.open_edit_prompt}}

Preserve identity, facial structure, hair, wardrobe, room and lighting from the reference image exactly. Change only expression, hand position and framing. Keep the eyes open and on the lens.

{{script.verdict_edit_prompt}}

Preserve identity, facial structure, hair, wardrobe, room and lighting from the reference image exactly. Change only expression, hand position and framing. Keep the eyes open and on the lens.

{{script.compare_card_prompt}}

Overhead flat-lay, vertical 9:16, plain matte surface, soft even daylight, real shadows under the objects, generous space between the two groups. Photographic, not illustrated. No lettering anywhere in frame.
nodes.negative_prompt: text, lettering, labels, logos, watermark, packaging copy, illustration, 3D render, busy background

nodes.prompt: Slow overhead drift across the flat-lay with a shallow rack of focus from the left group to the right group. A hand enters and taps the right-hand object once. Nobody speaks. No text appears.
nodes.negative_prompt: talking, speech, text overlay, subtitles, lettering, watermark, warped hands, extra fingers
